40_marg2213: Osee means “saviour.” The word of the Lord came to the prophet so that, by inspiring his mind, it might make him a god, and the saviour of his people, by announcing to them the words of God and giving them examples of good living. The saints to whom the word of the Lord comes are gods and saviours by grace, while there is one God and Saviour by nature, who was prefigured by all of them. So Hosea signifies Christ, the son of that well who says of himself: “They have forsaken me, the fountain of living water, and have digged to themselves cisterns that can hold no water.” For a well has waters flowing from a living spring; a cistern, waters brought in from outside, which it only keeps cool.
40_marg2214: Son of Beeri, “of my well”: that is, of the wells that Abraham and Isaac and Jacob dug, which the Philistines tried to stop up. A well has lasting waters flowing from a living spring; a cistern, waters brought in from outside, which it keeps cool. Hence: “They have forsaken me, the fountain of living water, and have digged to themselves cisterns that can hold no water”; and hence: “With thee is the fountain of life.”

40_marg2215: Jerome: These kings reigned over the people of God, whose name means “confession”; but in Israel, which had made idols for itself, reigned Jeroboam, whose name means chronismos, that is, temporality or delay, because he loved the world and strove to linger in the love of it, not seeking the world to come.
40_marg2216: Uzziah, also called Azariah, reigned in Jerusalem over the two tribes fifty-two years. His son Jotham succeeded him and reigned sixteen years; after him his son Ahaz, likewise sixteen years, in whose eleventh year the ten tribes were taken captive by Shalmaneser, king of the Assyrians (others say of the Chaldeans), and settled in the mountains of the Medes. After Ahaz reigned his son Hezekiah twenty-nine years. So it is plain that Hosea prophesied before the captivity, under Uzziah and Jotham; mourned it as it came on, under Ahaz; and told it over, when it was past, for the amendment of Judah, under King Hezekiah. At the time Uzziah began to reign over Judah, Jeroboam was in the twelfth year of his reign over Israel: the great-grandson of Jehu, to whom the Lord had promised that his sons would reign to the fourth generation, because he had killed Jezebel and two wicked kings, Joram king of Judah and Ahab king of Samaria, with his seventy brothers.
40_marg2217: “Hosea was of the tribe of Issachar, born in Belemoth. In his prophecy he gave a sign: ‘The Lord will come upon the earth like the oak that is in Shiloh,’ and so on. He was buried in his own land and sleeps in peaceful rest.” “He bears the figure of Christ, who out of the fornication of the Gentiles took the Church into his body.” He prophesied against the ten tribes, saying little of the two. He prophesied, as history, that the Jews would return to Christ in the last time. He also foretold the third day, of the Lord’s resurrection.
40_marg2218: By the surface of the story it seems strange that the Lord should command, or the prophet, commanded to take a harlot, should obey. But neither did the Lord command a shameful thing, nor did the prophet sin by obeying; rather he called the harlot back to chastity and, remaining in his own goodness, made her good from bad. What is done in him according to the flesh is done in God spiritually, who took the synagogue, forgetful of her husband and committing fornication with the many gods of the Gentiles. And note that in this prophet and in the others the coming of Christ and the calling of the Gentiles are so foretold that the root of the history, as the letter sounds, is not wholly abandoned, but what the prophet says fits his own time; lest he seem not to teach the assembly he speaks to about what it has in mind, but to play with things uncertain and to come. So the two women Hosea took, Gomer the harlot, who bore three children, and the other, who is hired for fifteen pieces of silver and called an adulteress, are referred to Israel and Judah.
40_marg2219: The prophets so promise the coming of Christ and the calling of the Gentiles that what they say fits the present time; lest they seem not to teach the assembly, called together for another purpose, about what it has in mind, but to play with things uncertain and to come. So here Gomer the daughter of Diblaim, whom Hosea marries and who bears a son named Jezreel, which means “seed of God,” in revenge for whose blood the kingdom of Jehu is overthrown, is to be referred to the calling of the Gentiles in a way that fits the time in which she is said to have borne the son. So these two women, Gomer the harlot, who bears three children, first Jezreel, second a girl called Without mercy, and third one called Not my people; and the other, who is hired for fifteen pieces of silver and a core and a half core of barley, and is called an adulteress, are referred to Israel and Judah. These are the two women who in Zechariah are said to have the wings of the hoopoe, the kite or the heron, and to go into the land of Shinar, where Babylon was built. Ezekiel signifies them under the names of two sisters, Aholah and Aholibah. These are the two sticks that Ezekiel joins into one stick.

40_marg2226: As to the letter, Jezreel is a chief city in the kingdom of the ten tribes, in which Naboth was killed; to avenge him Jehu was raised up, who destroyed Ahab and Jezebel. But because he and his sons afterwards turned to idolatry, his kingdom too is said to be overthrown. Under his great-grandson Jeroboam Hosea began to prophesy. When that Jeroboam died, his son Zechariah succeeded him, whom Shallum, born of another stock, killed in the sixth month of his reign; and at once the kings of Assyria took Reuben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh, which was beyond the Jordan, then Naphtali, and at last all the remaining tribes. From Zechariah, Jehu’s great-grandson, to Hoshea, under whom all the tribes were taken captive, were forty-nine years. But the figure of the seed of God and the vengeance for his blood are referred to the Lord’s passion, for which both the house of Judah and the kingdom of all Israel are said to be overthrown.
40_marg2227: CALL HIS NAME, and so on. This is as if he had said: Call his name Naboth, whose blood was to be avenged. And this is a figure of Christ, whose blood was to be avenged on those who crucified and mocked him.
40_marg2228: Jezreel is a chief city in the kingdom of Samaria, near which are very wide plains and a vast valley stretching more than ten thousand paces. There, when battle was joined, Israel, that is, the ten tribes, was cut down by the Assyrians. They are called Ephraim because of Jeroboam, born of Ephraim, who first made the schism in the people. They are called Joseph too, because Joseph was Ephraim’s father. They are called Samaria too, which was itself another chief city of the ten tribes, afterwards called by Augustus Augusta, that is, Sebaste, in which the bones of John the Baptist are laid. After the division of the ten tribes from the two, because of the very great multitude that followed Jeroboam, the old name Israel remained with the ten tribes; and because of the tribe of Judah, which reigned in Jerusalem, the two tribes are called Judah.

40_marg2241: Haimo: Show the synagogue that she who cast me off is no longer a lawful wife, and I will cast her off, so as not to be her husband. But that I may join her to myself again, I who am the husband of the soul, let her repent, at least after my coming in the flesh, of the uncleanness and fornication she practised with idols. Let her remove, then, the worship of idols from her love and her presence, for she lay open to the lust of many, worshipping the gods of all the nations. Let her take away her adulteries too from between her breasts, that is, from the heart, in which an evil deed is first conceived. For the heart is between the breasts, and from it come forth the thoughts which afterwards go on to deeds. So he exhorts her not to be deprived, for her crimes, of the grace given her by God. After the warning he adds the threat: Lest I strip her naked. The garment by which that people was ruled is understood as God’s help, the teaching of the law and the prophets, and the protection of the angels; all of which he threatens to take away unless she repents of her crime, so that she goes back to the day of her birth, that is, is made like the heathen. After the coming of the truth, even the observance of the law is counted as idolatry.

But now the sons will be taken captive with their fathers and will die outside the land of their birth, because they are children of fornication: for they were begotten in the worship of idols; the faith the fathers had, they handed on to their sons. Hence there follows: For their mother hath committed fornication. Viper bred viper; and she grew so shameless towards God that she sought glory in her crime, saying: I will go after my lovers, who give me what I need for food and clothing. It can also be referred to those who, denying the Son of God, chose the author of sedition. 40_marg2268: In memory of Belus was consecrated the idol called Bel, and by this name the prophets often call the idol of Babylon. The Sidonians often call him Baal or Baalim. Baal means “having,” Baalim “having me.” Hence women too call their husbands Baalim, that is, my husband, namely the one who has me in marriage. But in the Hebrew tongue a husband is called is, and a wife issa. So it is said here that the believing people, wishing to show me to be her husband, will call me is, that is, husband, not Baalim, which likewise means my husband: for though by its etymology it could be said, yet out of hatred of idols it ought not to be said, lest in the worship of God we recall the name of idols, and lest, while she names her husband, she think of the idol, as could happen through the ambiguity of the word. From this we learn that heresy can be incurred by words alone, carelessly uttered.

Third, at the coming of the Son, which is in the faith of the Trinity: believing in this faith, they know at once that he is God whom before they denied. So this harlot, who had been joined to the embraces of strange men, because she worshipped idols in Egypt, is taken again through the law; and because she transgressed it, killing the prophets as if they were the bridegroom’s companions, the Son came third; and when he had been crucified and had risen from the dead, she is espoused no longer in the justice of the law, but in faith, in the grace of the Gospel, and in the knowledge of the truth.

40_marg2272: Jerome: According to the letter it can be understood that at the coming of Christ temporal goods are promised to believers, so that, for his sake who is the seed of God, all things run in their order, as they were made from the beginning, and serve the good of men; and yet the Jews, after so many good things, still look in a carnal way for Antichrist. Spiritually, the heavens, which “shew forth the glory of God,” are heard when they ask for the Canaanite woman and for Peter’s mother-in-law; and the heavens hear the earth, that is, the men who are in the Church; and the earth hears the wheat, that is, it so gives the spiritual understanding of the Old and New Testament as to gladden the hearts of the hearers, measuring its teaching to their capacity. 40_marg2278: A CORE OF BARLEY, that is, thirty measures, and a half, that is, fifteen, which make forty-five measures: for this wage she is hired. On the fifteenth day of the month Nisan, which is March, the firstborn of the Egyptians were struck down, and Israel was brought out of Egypt and by this wage hired into the service of God; and for the firstborn of Israel, who did not feel the plague, fifteen shekels of silver are offered for the temple. On the forty-fifth day the people came to Mount Sinai, and at once, the next day, they are commanded to abstain from women, and, sanctified for three days, to prepare themselves to receive the law; and on the fiftieth day Moses received the ten commandments. Fittingly, then, they are said to be hired for forty-five measures of barley, who after the coming of Christ sit and wait for the coming of their husband, “until the fulness of the Gentiles should come in, and so all Israel should be saved”; who meanwhile neither has God nor serves idols, nor uses the food of men but the barley of beasts, because it has nothing spiritual in the law but follows the letter.

40_marg2285: From the beginning of the prophecy up to this place, under the description of the harlot and of the adulteress, who after heavy punishments and long abandonment are afterwards restored to their former or a better state, the sins of the ten tribes, or of the two tribes, and of all in common, are numbered. Now the discourse turns to the ten tribes, showing that God is not angry for nothing when he threatens and inflicts such heavy punishments; lest it seem to anyone that the sentence was brought unjustly on those who had not sinned, not from the truth of judgment but from the power of God. All this is referred most of all to those who would not receive Christ in the flesh, and to their descendants. With the inhabitants, that is, with the Jews who love earthly things, the Lord enters into judgment, condemning them, because he is not in them who says, “I am the truth.” And there is no mercy: they have mercy neither on the orphan nor on the widow, nor on Christ himself; and in their minds dwells no knowledge, that is, faith and the knowledge of God, or the very Wisdom of the Father. Cursing belongs to those who said, “Thou hast a devil”; lying, to those who said, “He is guilty of death”; killing, because they killed him and the prophets; theft, because they steal themselves and their children from God, saying, “His blood be upon us and upon our children”; adultery is referred to uncleanness or idolatry. Blood touches blood when sin is added to sin; for by the name of blood sin is signified.

40_marg2307: Allegorically: If you, heretic, play the harlot, at least let Judah, that is, the Church, not commit fornication; and let her not go into Galgal, that is, the gatherings of heretics, where the sins of all are laid bare: for Galgal means “revelation” or “wallowing-place,” and like swine they wallow in the mire of vices. For as a cow is stung by the gadfly, so the heretics are stung by the burning arrows of the devil, and have left the knowledge of the law; so they will feed in the broad way that leads to death, and the patience of the good shepherd fattens them for death.
40_marg2308: GALGAL is the place where Saul was anointed king, where also the people, coming from the desert, first encamped and were cleansed by the second circumcision; and from that time the error of a contrary religion grew up in that famous place. Bethaven was once called Bethel; but after the golden calves were set up there by Jeroboam, it is called not the house of God but the house of uselessness and the house of an idol. Perhaps the people of Israel in the wilderness made themselves a calf’s head to worship, and Jeroboam his golden images, for this reason: to keep in their superstition what they had learned among the Egyptians, who worship their gods under the figure of an ox.
